text:
> if you require attestation you don’t require any specific provider. I.e. ban vendor lock-in: if I have a key, I should be able to use it, and move my passkey to another one if I need to.

Unfortunately this is fundamentally at odds attestation: If you trust anybody capable of providing a syntactically valid signature, it's not attestation anymore.

You can try and set up a neutral clearinghouse vetting attestation providers, but that itself will probably become a centralizing force itself, requiring expensive audits etc. – think web PKI certificate authorities, but even more complex (as you need keys in shipped end user devices, not just somebody's data center HSMs).

I think shunning attestation is largely the right move, with a very short list of exceptions (high trust e-signatures, high value bank transactions but not daily payment confirmation etc.)

text:
Well, the exact same question applies to biology. If humans are conscious, is all life conscious? If it's just the brain that's conscious, is every part of the brain conscious? Are individual neurons conscious? How about other cells in your body, or tissues or organs? Our stomach has more cells and more neurons than many full animals - is our stomach conscious?

The answer in the "consciousness is a computation" model is that consciousness can arise in any computational medium. But the model doesn't say that any computation is conscious - it says that consciousness is any of a set of specific computations, any computation with properties X, Y, Z whatever. So it's perfectly possible (according to this model) that a GPU running game graphics is not conscious, while a GPU running some future even more advamced LLM is conscious. Or a network of GPUs + storage + whatever.
